findings.message: Cognitive Overload — Inline JS one-liner in nested shell quoting, while the file already has a heredoc pattern for this. Symptom: `scripts/verify.sh:152` puts a whole JS program on one line inside double quotes, then `bash -lc '…'`, then `node -e '\''…'\''`. Every JS string literal is written `\"…\"`, and the line ends in `'\'''"`. The same file already builds its browser probe with a heredoc and runs it as `node … -e ${browser_probe_js_escaped}` (`scripts/verify.sh:~370–390`). Source: Code Complete — layout should show logical structure. The Mythical Man-Month — Conceptual Integrity: one decision ("how do we run a Node probe in the container?") is made two different ways. Consequence: The next person who edits this, for example to add a field or change the config path, has to reason about three quoting layers at once. One misplaced `'` fails quietly as "Failed to inspect active Google Workspace credential route mode", which looks just like a real config error. A diff can't show it either: any edit rewrites the whole 600-character line. Remedy: Put the JS in a `read -r -d '' gws_route_js <<'NODE' … NODE` heredoc with normal formatting and quotes. Escape it with `printf '%q'` and call `gce_ssh_lastline "sudo docker exec ${container_escaped} node -e ${gws_route_js_escaped}"`, the same way the browser probe does. That also removes the `bash -lc` layer this probe doesn't need.

Knowledge Duplication — Validation of `credentialsFile` is split between the remote JS and the host-side jq. Symptom: The remote JS now turns a non-string `credentialsFile` into `null`. The host then checks it again with `jq -r '.credentialsFile | select(type == "string" and length > 0)'` (`scripts/verify.sh:157`). Route and mode are checked remotely, but the path is checked locally, and in a different language. Source: The Pragmatic Programmer — DRY: each piece of knowledge should have one authoritative place. Consequence: Change one side and not the other and the two stop agreeing. For example, if the JS starts allowing empty strings, the host-side check will still reject them. Remedy: Pick one place to own the shape check. Either have the JS output only what it has already validated and drop the host's `select`, or keep the JS as plain extraction and do all the checks in the host-side jq. ---
